einzeiler: Why your need for control drains you and how to find peace instead
kurzfassung: Lysa TerKeurst joins the podcast to discuss her new book, Making Peace With What I Can't Control, focusing on the exhaustion of trying to fix everything and manage outcomes. She examines the biblical story of Judas from a fresh perspective, exploring how his desire for immediate control and a political Messiah mirrors our own tendency to force outcomes. Ultimately, TerKeurst explains the shift from a control mindset to a stewardship mindset of taking responsibility while trusting God with the results.
stichpunkte: Lysa TerKeurst introduces her upcoming book, Making Peace With What I Can't Control, addressing overthinking, trying to fix others, and the exhaustion of wanting to figure everything out.
The conversation examines Chapter 3 of the book, which looks at Judas not as a villain in our personal stories, but as an example of someone who tried to force a specific outcome.
Scholars suggest Judas betrayed Jesus because Jesus was not acting as the military leader and political Messiah the Jewish people wanted to overthrow Roman oppression.
Judas wanted immediate relief and victory, whereas Jesus offered eternal rescue and spiritual salvation.
Judas addressed Jesus as Rabbi rather than Lord, reflecting a reluctance to submit to Jesus's actual kingship over his life.
TerKeurst highlights the danger of fooling oneself into thinking one is helping God rather than trusting Him.

The difference between a control mindset and a stewardship mindset is contrasted: control uses closed fists to force preferred outcomes, while stewardship means managing personal responsibilities and trusting God with the results.
TerKeurst emphasizes that acknowledging mistakes and surrendering to God brings grace rather than condemnation.

kapitel.titel: The Biblical Perspective on Judas and Control

clips.hook: It's not a power thing for me. It really is a fear thing.
clips.text: The author explains that her struggle with control stems not from a desire for power, but from a fear of negative outcomes and emotional suffering.

clips.hook: I've cooked the meal, but now we all have to sit at the table and eat it.
clips.text: Writing a book on a topic does not mean the author has perfected it; she still needs to apply its lessons to her own life daily.

beschreibung:
Are you feeling worn out from constantly overthinking, trying to fix the people around you, or attempting to figure out every detail of your future? In this episode, hosts Kaley Olson and Cailah Garcia sit down with Proverbs 31 Ministries President Lysa TerKeurst for an exclusive preview of her book Making Peace with What I Can't Control. Together, they unpack an unexpected aspect in the story of Judas in Matthew 26, revealing how a subtle desire to force immediate relief can lead us to take control into our own hands rather than trust God. Listen in to discover how making one foundational shift in perspective can help you release the weight you were never meant to carry and bring true rest to your heart today.

You’ll learn:
How Judas’ story highlights our own tendency to try to control the details when God doesn't move on our timeline.
Practical ways to stop wasting mental energy on managing other people's choices and circumstances that are out of your hands.
How to shift from a high-pressure control mindset to a healthy stewardship mindset that surrenders ultimate outcomes to God.
